body: Hurdle 1.7623x = 1.12^5 (index CAGR, not CoE 12.5% = 1.802x; no explicit margin of safety). Class share reaching >=1.76x in 5y: India non-fin 49.6% (median 1.69x, mean 2.24x; 2016 start 39%, 2018 start 59%); India lenders 33.6% (median 1.04x); US float 28.4% vs own 1.47x hurdle 38.2%. Hurdle consistent with classes. Mechanics: (a) EV gate treats scenario mult5 as mean while probabilities/Kelly treat it as lognormal median (gap e^{sigma^2/2}, ~6-8%); Kelly turns positive before the EV gate on every card; (b) anchoring imports class left tails only, not P(>=3x) (model P(>=3x) 0.4-10% vs base 21%); (c) all 6 cards weight bear > bull. Synthetic India: fair firm (base IRR = CoE 12.5%) anchored EV 1.63-1.66x -> size 0; good firm (CoE+5pp) 2.02-2.06x -> 4% cap. Effective pass line ~13.8-14.3% base IRR (vs 12% without anchoring). Live cards: base IRRs 3-11%, all below CoE; price fall needed for EV gate HARSHA 14%, INDRAMEDCO 19%, AUTOAXLES 21%, SUNFLAG 22%, US-KEX 24%, UTKARSHBNK 33%. Verdict: partial structural bias (~2pp undeclared margin of safety); zeros mostly genuine on our own inputs; fair=0 by construction so 6/6 zeros say nothing about market fairness. Candidate fixes (NOT applied; pre-register before Jan-Feb 2027 scoring): consistent mean/median convention, explicit margin of safety, two-sided anchoring, sigma toward class dispersion, scenario-shape flag, warn on null deprecated class (US-KEX).
title: Stage-6 audit: is the decision card a 'no machine'? Partial: good firms pass, fair firms never do; 6 live zeros are mostly genuine
